requirements.rule: A laterally extensive, comparatively smooth floor-like unit is visible in or adjoining the 20 km footprint. Brightness alone cannot establish flatness or a basin origin.
An organized ridge, scarp or mass-defined margin is visible within 80 km context. It need not share an impact or depositional origin with the target.

sources.title: Bristol Dry Lake, California: An Analog for Ancient Lacustrine Environments on Mars
sources.finding: Bristol Dry Lake was explicitly proposed as a Mars lacustrine analogue before this study. The new Mojave window lies in the same broader basin setting; its 80km context cannot be called an undiscovered Mars analogue region.

sources.title: Studies of a Lacustrine-Volcanic Mars Analog Field Site With Mars-2020-Like Instruments
sources.access: Publisher abstract and indexed full text; later repeated fetch timed out
sources.finding: Prior Mojave Mars-2020 instrument and geological mapping work defeats a broad first-Mojave mapping claim. Exact spatial overlap with this footprint was not established.

sources.title: Biosignatures in Precambrian and Cambrian Carbonate Rich Sedimentary Sequences of Anti-Atlas, Morocco
sources.access: Primary conference abstract indexed text reviewed
sources.finding: The Anti-Atlas has an explicit prior Jezero/Midway material and biosignature association. This is not ground truth for terrain mapping, but prevents a broad new Anti-Atlas/Jezero claim.

sources.title: Regional Structural Geology of Earth and Mars
sources.access: Full 273-page thesis acquired locally; introduction, abstract, relevant sections and synthesis checked
sources.finding: Quinn studied the southern Naukluft and northeast Syrtis using regional structural mapping. The synthesis compares northeast Syrtis with Namibian Neoproterozoic records. Our Syrtis window is a different southern volcanic context, but broad Namibia/Syrtis mapping novelty is not defensible from search absence.

sources.title: Introducing the Mapboard GIS iPad app
sources.finding: Existing digital mapping workflow includes Namibian field geology. Software-assisted regional mapping on Earth and Mars is established practice.

sources.title: To Titan, via Namibia
sources.access: Indexed original abstract; direct full-text request failed
sources.finding: Namib landforms already have planetary analogue uses, particularly dunes. This is a prior regional association, not proof of the exact Syrtis mapping task.

sources.title: Detection of biosignatures in Terrestrial analogs of Martian regions
sources.access: Publisher abstract and indexed table reviewed
sources.finding: Broad Namib, Atacama, Qaidam and other terrestrial Mars analogue settings are known; morphology alone cannot establish biosignature transfer.

limits: Crossref search is relevance-ranked metadata retrieval, not an exhaustive bibliographic search.
No assertion that every returned full text was acquired or read.
No complete spatial intersection audit of all published geological units and footprints.
Different grid centers, weights, descriptors or ranking code alone do not establish analogue novelty.
Unpublished campaigns, non-indexed work and inaccessible catalogues remain possible.

claim_reviews.assessor: Codex model-assisted literature review, not an independent librarian or geologist
claim_reviews.rationale: The separately acquired optical observations support the frozen coarse floor/margin mapping rubric. Prior regional analogue studies are documented, so this release adds a reproducible characterization while exact-footprint/task novelty remains unresolved.
